newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia 1st quarter real tax receipts 49 pct target.
newsitem.headline: Russia 1st quarter real tax receipts 49 pct target.

text.p: Russia collected 69 percent of targeted taxes on paper in the first quarter of this year, but actual receipts made up only 49 percent of budget tax revenues, Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov said on Wednesday.

"Debt cancellation in the first quarter was 44.2 percent of total tax receipts. Real receipts in the first quarter were a total 25.0 trillion roubles after 25.8 trillion in that period last year," he told a meeting of the State Tax Service.
He said total tax receipts were 68.7 percent of target but that real receipts were only 48.7 percent of target.
Debt cancellation is possible since the government and businesses owe each other millions of dollars in a tangled web of non-payments.

In addition to the non-payments issue, Russia has had difficulty collecting taxes, a primary reason the International Monetary fund has delayed a few tranches of its three-year $10 billion loan to Russia.
"If debt cancellation (as payment) exceepts 50 percent, the government is on the edge of bankruptcy," Kulikov warned.
Kulikov was put in charge of enforcing tax collection and fighting tax evasion earlier this year.
New State Tax Service head Alexander Pochinok told a news conference he hoped to improve tax collection to 90 percent by the end of the first half.
Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais said last week that first quarter receipts for the entire budget were 56.6 percent.
